what_happened: Re-measurement found the dispatch's own at-creation figure (22 resolve_candidate callers) undercounted the true population by more than half: a third, grep-invisible shape (inline CANDIDATES-array for-loop, 38 suites) implements the identical deploy-tree-first/source-store-fallback pattern without ever naming a function resolve_candidate. True family size is 70 of 144 scripts/tests/*.sh suites, not 22/60/119 nor the stale doc's 41/73.

Direct inspection of common_test_resolve_candidate call sites found the implicit resolution order is NOT uniformly deploy-tree-first even today: test-gate-out-derived-staleness.sh and test-install-uninstall-extension.sh both pass the source-store candidate first. Confirms the preference is caller-specific and currently undeclared/unaudited, exactly the defect the dispatch describes -- not a single uniform default that merely needs documenting.

Plan-time territory scan found scripts/tests/test-lint-dead-command-recommendations.sh is both in this task's 70-suite migration family (Group A) and in concurrent sibling task 512's declared file_scope for this same cycle. Declared it in Phase 3's Files to modify so the admission gate serializes the two tasks rather than silently excluding the file, with a re-read-before-edit step and an allowlist-deferral contingency in Rollback.

Every population figure in the research report (144 total suites, 70 family, 20 shared-helper / 12 local-duplicate / 38 inline-loop, 3 deployed-only) reproduced byte-for-byte at plan-authoring time from the report's own Appendix commands, so the plan's phase batching could be built on measured file lists instead of estimates. The report's reproducible-commands appendix is what made that cheap.
